g.title: sic_micro_prior_setting_degree → icts_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio intra_scale A newly infected agent's prior same-setting contact degree can shape how many contacts are available for notification and how the agent's behavior changes when later quarantined; greater prior connectedness may imply a larger pre-onset contact set and a different potential post-onset contact reduction, thereby affecting the observed post/pre contact ratio.

g.title: icts_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio → sic_micro_prior_setting_degree intra_scale Quarantine onset and the associated reduction in an agent's contacts remove that agent from ongoing setting-level mixing; this changes the pool and connectivity of remaining contacts available to susceptible agents, altering the prior same-setting contact degree observed for later infection events in those settings.

g.title: sic_meso_layer_infection_contact_ratio → icts_meso_layer_contact_change intra_scale A layer with more infection events per observed contact row can trigger more detection, tracing, and quarantine activity associated with that setting; when city quarantine counts rise, this can produce larger reductions in contact volume within that layer because more agents linked to the layer are removed or reduce activity.

g.title: icts_meso_layer_contact_change → sic_meso_layer_infection_contact_ratio intra_scale Quarantine-associated reductions in a layer's contact volume change the density and mixing pattern of remaining contacts; this alters both the contact-row denominator and the likelihood that infection events occur per remaining contact row within that layer.

g.title: sic_macro_layer_entropy → icts_macro_city_contact_change_on_quarantine_increase intra_scale A more dispersed or concentrated distribution of infection events across layers indicates which settings are driving transmission; this changes which settings generate quarantine increases and how city-level contact volume changes when quarantine counts rise.

g.title: icts_macro_city_contact_change_on_quarantine_increase → sic_macro_layer_entropy intra_scale City contact-volume changes on quarantine-increase steps can reduce contacts unevenly across layers; by suppressing mixing in some settings more than others, these changes reshape the relative occurrence of infection events across settings and therefore the layer entropy of infection events.

The indicator value for e is D(e). W is a pre-specified nonnegative integer window length. g.title: N2 | sic_meso_layer_infection_contact_ratio Layer-specific infection events per contact edge Scale: meso | Phenomenon: setting_infection_clustering Definition: For run r, layer L, window [s,s+W-1], let I(r,L,s)=# { e in events : e.run_id=r, e.layer=L, e.step in [s,s+W-1], e classified as an infection transition }, and C(r,L,s)=# { c in contacts : c.run_id=r, c.layer=L, c.step in [s,s+W-1] }. g.title: N4 | icts_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio Agent contact-degree ratio around quarantine onset Scale: micro | Phenomenon: intervention_contact_trajectory_shift Definition: For each event q in events with run_id r, step s, agent_id a, state matching the observed quarantined label, before=false, after=true, let P_pre={p: exists c in contacts, c.run_id=r, c.step in [s-W,s-1], ((c.agent_id=a and c.partner_id=p) or (c.partner_id=a and c.agent_id=p)), p non-null/non-sentinel, p!=a} and P_post similarly for c.step in [s+1,s+W]. Indicator = |P_post|/|P_pre| if |P_pre|>0; undefined if |P_pre|=0. The supplied onset/contacts data do not trigger the latter conditions; the observation-unit mismatch remains. Not executed.'}}

g.title: N5 | icts_meso_layer_contact_change Layer contact-volume change around quarantine-count increase Scale: meso | Phenomenon: intervention_contact_trajectory_shift Definition: For run r and layer L, let Q_t=model_states.quarantined at step t. Let S={t: Q_t>Q_prev(t) with previous sampled step observed}. For each t in S, define C_pre(t)=mean over u in [t-W,t-1] intersect observed steps of # contacts rows with run_id=r, layer=L, step=u; C_post(t)=mean over u in [t+1,t+W] intersect observed steps of # contacts rows with run_id=r, layer=L, step=u. Indicator = median over t in S of (C_post(t)-C_pre(t)) when S and required pre/post steps exist; undefined if S is empty or no pre/post observed steps exist. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'success', 'series_file': 'indicator_series/3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae/icts_meso_layer_contact_change.parquet', 'series_sha256': '934dfd6236571bae46827252f2c92b21559b1122e23d155b7b080b99b7fbd537'}}

g.title: N6 | icts_macro_city_contact_change_on_quarantine_increase City contact-volume change on quarantine-increase steps Scale: macro | Phenomenon: intervention_contact_trajectory_shift Definition: For run r, let C_t=# contacts rows at step t; DeltaC_t=C_t-C_{t-1}; DeltaQ_t=Q_t-Q_{t-1} from model_states.quarantined. Let A=mean{DeltaC_t: DeltaQ_t>0 and both t and t-1 are observed}; B=mean{DeltaC_t: DeltaQ_t=0 and both t and t-1 are observed}. Indicator=A-B. Undefined if A or B has no members.
